chunks: You are being chased by death. If you stop, it will catch you, and if you run away from it, it will grip you. It is more attached to you than your shadow. Death is tied to your fore-locks while the world is being wrapped up from behind you. Therefore, fear the Fire whose hollow is deep, whose flames are severe and whose punishment is novel. It is a place wherein there is no mercy. No call is heard in it. No pain is healed in it.

key_terms.طُرَدَاءُ الْمَوْتِ: Chased by death / Death as a pursuer
key_terms.كُرْبَةٌ: Distress/Pain (specifically in the context of the afterlife)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of death being described as 'tied to the forelocks' in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this address to his son Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr upon his appointment as governor of Egypt, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) uses the metaphor of death as an inescapable pursuer to underscore the urgency of spiritual readiness amidst worldly power. He contrasts the fleeting nature of the dunya, which 'unfurls behind' the believer, with the permanence of the Hereafter, warning that true security lies not in political authority but in mindfulness of the severe, enduring punishment of Hellfire.
